title: Latency Cadenza: route+model percentile skyline with streaming vs non-streaming cohorts
creator: Priya Desai
description: Goal: Deliver a single interactive dashboard (Latency Cadenza) that surfaces p50/p95/p99 latency for every model-route pair with a clear split between streaming and non-streaming (blocking) IO modes, and correlates spikes with trace hooks and error counts. The board should enable engineers and SREs to: 1) rapidly identify whether regressions are driven by specific models, routes, or by IO mode; 2) drill into traces and logs from the panel; 3) generate cohort comparisons (time-of-day, request-shape, seq-length buckets); and 4) wire alerting rules for sustained percentile drift. This is intended to be a production-facing SLI/diagnostic board for both hosted API and Dedicated customers.
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard exposes p50/p95/p99 for model x route tuples over selectable windows (1h, 6h, 24h, 7d)
Streaming vs Non-streaming series visible side-by-side and as stacked deltas; toggleable UI
Per-cohort filters: model version, route name, region, tenant type (hosted/dedicated), request token-length bucket
Each percentile datapoint links to trace sample(s) via trace_id with at least one trace captured when an SLI breach occurs
Error-rate overlay and a per-model error-count heatmap panel is present
Query performance: board panels load within 3s for 24h queries and 6s for 7d queries under normal load
Automated test harness runs nightly validating panel queries against telemetry schema and synthetic traces
Alerts created: p95 > 800ms for 5m sustained OR p99 > 2s for 3m; alert runbooks linked
Ownership documented and dashboard added to runbook and console dashboard registry
implementation_notes: Data sources: metrics from metrics-pipeline (request.latency.histogram) + tags {model, model_version, route, io_mode, region, tenant_id}
Streaming identification: use io_mode tag (streaming|blocking); fallback to response_mode when io_mode missing
Percentile computation: use histogram aggregation (hdr or native summary depending on TSDB) to avoid p99 tail sampling bias
Tracing: ensure trace hook attaches trace_id to top slow requests; extend existing tracing middleware to capture 'servepath_segment' and 'kv_cache_hit' tags
Logs: add structured log fields request_shape and prompt_tokens to pipeline to support cohorting in panel
Query hints: pre-aggregate 1m windows for long range queries to keep panel latency under threshold
Panel visuals: skyline area charts for p50/p95/p99 with small-multiples by model, stacked delta bar for streaming vs non-streaming, and a heatmap of p99 anomalies by route
Feature flags: rollout behind 'latency_cadenza_v1' so we can enable for internal users then tenants gradually
Privacy: strip tenant identifiers in shared views; provide a tenant-scoped view for Dedicated customers only
work_items: extend metrics exporter to include io_mode and model_version tags (ENG-568124)
add trace hook to serving runtime with servepath_segment and kv_cache_hit tags (ENG-568125)
update metrics-aggregation config to pre-aggregate percentiles for 1m/5m/1h windows (ENG-568126)
synthetic test generator to emit streaming+blocking traffic (ENG-568127)
QA: cross-validate p99 against raw traces for 24h synthetic run
risks_and_mitigations: High cardinality when joining model_version, route, and tenant -> mitigate with cardinality caps and rollups; refuse to render > 200 series
Percentile divergence between histogram summaries and raw traces -> nightly job to surface mismatches and adjust aggregation windows
Dashboard query cost -> pre-aggregate and cache; use cheaper approximate histograms for long windows
Missing io_mode tags on older clients -> fallback heuristics and a small retrograde job to backfill where feasible
testing_plan: Unit tests for histogram aggregation and query templates
Integration test: end-to-end synthetic traffic generator validates UI percentiles against synthetic trace-derived percentiles
Load test: simulate 100 simultaneous dashboard queries to measure backend impact
Canary rollout: enable behind feature flag for internal SREs for 72 hours, gather feedback, then opt-in 10% tenants
rollout_plan: Week 1: instrumentation changes (metrics exporter + trace hook) + unit tests
Week 2: pre-aggregations + dashboard scaffolding; internal QA
Week 3: internal canary (SRE), fix issues; add alerts and runbooks
Week 4: staged tenant rollout; monitor cost and OOM indicators; full launch end of Week 4
